newsitem.title: FRANCE: EDF to enter French telecoms market - minister.
newsitem.headline: EDF to enter French telecoms market - minister.

text.p: French telecommunications minister Francois Fillon said in an interview to appear on Thursday that the government did not want a telecoms duopoly in France and it expected electricity utility Electricite de France (EDF) to move in as another player.

"In the coming months (EdF) will announce its strategy in this field. EdF will be a player in the telecoms infrastructure market, the government wants this," Fillon said in an interview for the Thursday edition of Les Echos.
An advance copy of the interview was supplied to Reuters.

On February 12, the SNCF state railways said it had chosen conglomerate Generale des Eaux's Cegetel telecoms unit to become its industrial partner for the operation of a telecoms network to rival France Telecom, choosing Cegetel over Bouygues Telecom.
Generale des Eaux is controlling partner in Cegetel and has British Telecom, Germany's Mannesmann, and SBC Communications Inc as partners.
